html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MCP: Model Context Protocol; API: application programming interface

  • Why the tool description is the main thing Claude uses to pick a tool
  • What a good description contains, and how to fix overlapping tools
  • The MCP isError pattern and structured error metadata
  • Error categories, retryable versus non-retryable, and access failure versus valid empty result

2Tool Descriptions Drive Tool Selection (Task 2.1)

Running case

Birchwood Supply's Agent Picks the Wrong Tool

  • Customers write: "is the blue kettle, item K-2210, in stock?"
  • The agent keeps calling find_product instead of check_stock
  • Both tools are described in three words ("Finds product information", "Gets stock details") and take similar identifiers
  • Claude decides which tool to call mainly from the tool's name, description and input schema. Minimal descriptions leave it guessing between similar tools.
  • A strong description states: what it does, expected input formats, example queries it should handle, edge cases and boundaries ("use this for X, not for Y: use check_stock for availability").

Weak Strong
check_stock: "Gets stock details" check_stock: "Returns units on hand and the restock date for ONE item. Input: an item code like K-2210 (letter, dash, four digits). Use for availability questions. Do NOT use to search by name or description: use find_product for that. Returns not_found if the code does not exist."

Fixing overlap

  • Ambiguous or overlapping descriptions cause misrouting (two tools such as analyze_content and analyze_document with near-identical text).
  • Rename and rewrite to remove the overlap: analyze_content → extract_web_results, with a web-specific description.
  • Split a generic tool into purpose-specific tools with defined input and output contracts: analyze_document → extract_data_points, summarize_content, verify_claim_against_source.
  • Check the system prompt for keyword-sensitive wording that can override good descriptions and create unintended tool associations (for example, a line that says "when the user mentions an item, always call find_product").
Exam tip

"Most effective first step" for wrong tool choice between similar tools → expand the descriptions (formats, examples, edge cases, boundaries). Few-shot examples (extra tokens), a pre-routing layer (over-engineered) and merging the tools (more effort) are not the first step.

Exam tip

Ambiguous or overlapping descriptions cause misrouting: rename, split into purpose-specific tools or rewrite them, and check the system prompt for keyword traps.

3Structured Error Responses (Task 2.2)

An MCP tool signals failure with the isError flag on its result so the agent knows the call failed; the content should say why, in a form the agent can act on.

Error category Examples Retry? What the agent should do
Transient Timeout, service unavailable Yes (with backoff) Retry, then try an alternative or report partial results
Validation Bad input format, missing field After fixing the input Correct the argument and call again
Business (policy) Refund window expired, limit exceeded No (retriable: false) Explain to the customer in plain words, or escalate
Permission Not allowed to access this record No (unless access changes) Stop and escalate or ask for authorization 
{
  "isError": true,
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{\"errorCategory\":\"business\",\"isRetryable\":false,\"message\":\"The 30-day return window closed on 4 March.\",\"customerMessage\":\"This item is outside our 30-day return window, but I can connect you with a specialist.\"}" }]
}

  • Why generic errors hurt: a plain "Operation failed" hides whether to retry, fix the input, or stop. The agent wastes retries or gives up too early.
  • Structured metadata (errorCategory, isRetryable, a human-readable description) lets the agent choose the right recovery, and prevents wasted retry attempts.
  • For business rule violations include retriable: false and a customer-friendly explanation the agent can pass on.
  • Local recovery first: a subagent should retry transient failures itself and propagate to the coordinator only what it cannot resolve, together with partial results and what was attempted (Module 13).

Access failure versus valid empty result

Access failure Valid empty result
Meaning The query could not be completed (timeout, auth) The query ran fine and found no matches
Signal isError: true with category Success with an empty list
Agent behavior Decide: retry, alternative, partial Report "nothing found" as a real answer

Exam tip

Returning an empty result as success when a timeout happened is an anti-pattern: the agent will conclude that nothing exists.

4Exam Q&A

S1The agent often calls find_product when shoppers ask whether an item code is in stock, instead of check_stock. Both tools have one-line descriptions and accept similar identifiers. What is the most effective first step?

  • AExpand each description with input formats, example queries, edge cases and boundaries against the similar tool
  • BMerge both tools into one lookup_entity tool
  • CAdd eight few-shot examples to the system prompt
  • DBuild a keyword router that pre-selects the tool each turn from patterns in the message
Show the answer

Answer: A. Descriptions are the primary selection mechanism, so improving them is the low-effort, high-leverage fix. The other options add tokens, infrastructure or redesign work before the root cause is addressed.

S2Two tools, analyze_content and analyze_document, have nearly identical descriptions and are often confused. Which fix is best?

  • AGive both tools exactly the same description so that the choice between them becomes random
  • BKeep the names and add "be careful" to the system prompt
  • CRename one to something specific such as extract_web_results and rewrite both descriptions to remove the overlap
  • DRemove one tool and handle both jobs by prompt
Show the answer

Answer: C. Renaming and rewriting removes the functional overlap that causes misrouting.

S3A generic analyze_document tool is used for extraction, summaries and fact checks, with inconsistent results. How should it be redesigned?

  • AAdd a second generic tool
  • BAdd a free-form mode string to the tool and hope that Claude chooses it well each time
  • CSplit it into purpose-specific tools with defined input and output contracts
  • DIncrease the model temperature
Show the answer

Answer: C. Specific tools with clear contracts (for example extract_data_points, summarize_content, verify_claim_against_source) are easier for the model to select and use correctly.

S4Well-written tool descriptions exist, yet the agent keeps preferring one tool whenever the user says "item". The system prompt says: "When the user mentions an item, call find_product first." What is the likely cause?

  • AThe tool schemas are so long that Claude cannot read all of them
  • BThe tool names are too short for Claude to tell them apart reliably
  • CThe API does not support two tools
  • DKeyword-sensitive system prompt wording biases tool choice
Show the answer

Answer: D. Review system prompts for wording that overrides tool descriptions.

S5A tool call fails with a timeout. Which tool result best supports recovery?

  • AA successful result with an empty list, so that the agent keeps going without errors
  • B"Operation failed"
  • CAn empty string
  • DA structured error: category transient, isRetryable: true, plus a description
Show the answer

Answer: D. Structured metadata tells the agent that retrying makes sense. A generic message hides the choice, and an empty success would be treated as "no data".

S6A refund request is rejected because the return window has closed. What should the tool return?

  • AA business error with isRetryable: false and a customer-friendly explanation
  • BA success with an empty body, because a policy decision is not a technical failure
  • CA transient error with isRetryable: true, so the agent tries the refund again later
  • DA permission error
Show the answer

Answer: A. A policy violation is a business error that must not be retried; the explanation lets the agent communicate it well.

S7A search tool returns zero matches for an existing customer's order history. How should the agent treat this?

  • AAs proof the tool is broken
  • BAs an access failure that requires several retries with exponential backoff
  • CAs a valid empty result, a successful query with no matches
  • DAs a permission error
Show the answer

Answer: C. A successful query with no matches is a real answer; do not confuse it with failure.

S8A subagent hits a brief network timeout on a search. What is the best behavior?

  • AAsk the human to retry manually
  • BRetry locally; if it still fails, propagate what was attempted and any partial results
  • CImmediately fail the whole workflow
  • DHide the timeout and return an empty result marked as success so the whole workflow can continue
Show the answer

Answer: B. Resolve transient problems locally and escalate only what cannot be resolved, with context.

S9Which field combination in an error result prevents wasted retries on a permission failure?

  • AisError: false with a free-text note that explains the permission problem
  • BisRetryable: true for every error
  • COnly a stack trace
  • DisError: true, errorCategory: "permission", isRetryable: false
Show the answer

Answer: D. Category and retryable flag let the agent stop retrying and escalate instead.

S10Which TWO changes most improve selection between two similar tools? Select TWO.

  • AReturn only "Operation failed" on errors
  • BRename both tools to tool1 and tool2
  • CAdd input formats and example queries to each description
  • DRemove the descriptions so the model is not biased
  • EState boundaries that say when to use the other tool instead
Show the answer

Answer: C, E. Clear formats, examples and boundaries differentiate tools. Removing text, meaningless names and generic errors make selection and recovery harder.

S11Which TWO pieces of metadata should a failed tool call return to guide recovery? Select TWO.

  • AThe server's internal address
  • BOnly a raw stack trace
  • CWhether the error is retryable
  • DAn error category such as transient or business
  • EA random request number
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. A category and a retryable flag tell the agent whether to retry, fix the input or stop. The other items do not support a recovery decision.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Selection signal The tool description (plus name and schema) is the primary mechanism
Good description Purpose · input formats · example queries · edge cases · boundaries vs similar tools
Overlap fixes Rename + rewrite; split generic tools; check system prompt for keyword-sensitive wording
First step Better descriptions before few-shot, routers or merging
Error flag MCP isError (API: is_error in tool_result)
Categories Transient (retry) · validation (fix input) · business (retriable:false, friendly text) · permission
Metadata errorCategory, isRetryable, human-readable description
Empty vs failure Access failure = error; no matches = valid empty success
Local recovery Subagent retries transient errors; propagates only the unresolved, with partial results
